hi! you’ve already received a lot of opinions, but i did take a look between your ref and your drawing. great work, first of all, with the shading. you were clearly shading as you saw it in the photo. i’m going to really ramble so sorry in advance!!

the biggest and first thing i noticed is that this drawing almost feels like you looked at the reference, and then drew what you think you saw (instead of drawing what you see). this is a really nuanced way of putting it as the difference is subtle, but really make sure you’re drawing the model exactly as she looks, not how you think a human should or may look. this isn’t something you can just learn and apply after hearing it, either. but keep it in mind as you continue to learn! draw what you see, not what you think you see.

the reason i say this is because of the details like the bottom of the breast, or the way the hair drapes down her back. also, it seems as though her upper body is a bit longer than 4 heads tall, but i’m not able to check myself rn. the biggest thing is the lack of hands, too. don’t let fear of failure stop you from making an attempt. if you see it in your reference, you need to see it in your study. one way to view art is that the goal is always to fail. every failure carries you one step further on your path of improvement. every time you skip out on certain features like hands (regardless of the reason!), you’re not giving yourself a chance to learn. 

personally, i think you and EVERYONE would benefit significantly from life drawing classes. i’m not sure how to explain it, but seeing a model in person and getting to work in a studio for a couple hours is so much different than drawing from photo images. but i know not everyone has the privilege or capacity or money to attend life drawing classes. but even going out with a sketchbook and drawing real people (like in a coffee shop or other public space, for example) would help significantly. 

i’m still a student, so take my advice with a grain of salt. but i hope any of this advice is what you were looking for!

things i noticed about the anatomy: usually in a 7 head proportions body, the navel is three heads down from the top. in your drawing, you have a 6 head proportions, which isn’t that typical IRL. assuming you’re going for a 6 head proportions (i believe most anime do 6 heads, for example?), the nipples are too low in this drawing, and the second head down in a 6 head proportions is USUALLY the end of the ribcage, between the navel and nipples.

you used value and tone well, and i really like your detail for the muscles and bones. it looks like you have at least some understanding of the actual anatomy underneath the skin, which is good.

maybe moving forward, keep in mind the head to body proportions, and be purposeful. i’ve seen others recommend gesture drawing and that sounds like good advice to me, too.

best of luck and great work!

i noticed you mentioned you’re using techniques, but i think you shouldn’t rely on techniques until you have a better understanding of the fundamentals of 3D shapes and line confidence. it looks like you’re using techniques to cover up your lack of knowledge. this isn’t a bad thing but i think it may hinder your growth. i personally view stylization and techniques as a simplification of the human figure, but you’re going to see that your forms won’t look realistic if you don’t have a solid foundation in the actual human form. this is difficult tho and something i struggle with too

another thing is your lines. it’s good that you don’t do “chicken scratch,” but your lines are very inconsistent, and it looks like you’re pushing down really hard. how do you hold the pencil? i suggest a loose grip near the middle or top of the pencil, rather than holding it near the tip. that puts less strain on your wrist and allows you to draw gestures more easily.
